explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: Silicon Data SDH100RT $2.96/hr on Nov 4, flat on Nov 3 and up 4c from $2.92 Oct 31; +2.1% on the week (Oct 28 $2.90). Another new high.
indicators.why: Rents kept rising through a week of AI-stock selling; renters are still paying more for compute.
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if SDH100RT prints below about $2.00 for a month or spot drops under the 1-yr contract rate. CFTC review of CME GPU futures ends Nov 9.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 31: +4c to $2.96. Page's '+5.0% 7d' is really Oct 6 to Nov 4; FAQ still stale at $2.53.

indicators.name: B200 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index) and B200/H100 ratio
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 $6.53 on Nov 4, down 11c from the Oct 31 high of $6.64 but +0.9% on the week (Oct 28 $6.47). B200/H100 ratio 2.21x (6.53/2.96). Both above the $4.50 and 2x triggers.
indicators.why: Oct 31 spike faded but the price holds above the prior week; the premium over H100 narrowed slightly as H100 kept climbing.
indicators.watch: Bearish if B200 drops below $4.50 or the ratio falls under 2x; Rubin availability capping Blackwell premiums.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 31: -11c to $6.53; ratio 2.21x from 2.27x; trend to flat. Page's '+11.2% 7d' not supported by its own table; FAQ stale at $5.45.

indicators.name: Hopper residual value: A100 index floor, used H100 prices, GPU useful-life accounting
indicators.value: A100 index $1.58 Nov 4, up 2c from $1.56 (Oct 28-Nov 1); 8c above the $1.50 floor. H200 $3.51 (from $3.47). No new useful-life cut found.
indicators.why: The oldest GPU in the index is edging away from the floor; residual value is firming, not breaking.
indicators.watch: A100 under $1.50; CoreWeave Q3 (Nov 10) depreciation life or Hopper impairment; Nvidia Nov 17.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 28: A100 +2c, H200 +4c. Page's '+3.9% 7d' not supported by the table (about +1.3%).

indicators.name: Data-centre cost of capital and build cost (10-yr Treasury, oil, $/GW)
indicators.value: 10-yr Treasury about 4.90-4.93% Nov 4, down from about 4.96% on election day; touched about 4.89%, lowest since early September. US crude down more than 8% Nov 4. Build cost still near $50B per GW (Huang, Oct 21).
indicators.why: Cheaper money and oil help build economics, but the same election raised permitting and power-cost risk for new sites, so the net is neutral.
indicators.watch: 10-yr back above 5.30% or below 4.75%; Nov 6 jobs and Nov 10 CPI; December hike odds (about 77%).
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 30: yield little changed net at about 4.9% but oil fell sharply on Iran-war pressure after the vote.

indicators.name: Memory prices: DRAM spot and contract (TrendForce), HBM
indicators.value: TrendForce spot Nov 4: DDR5 16Gb $61.33 (-0.27%), DDR4 16Gb $81.93 (-0.96%). Contract table still 2H Sep: DDR4 16Gb $52.00 (+4.0%). October contract update (Oct 30) not shown in the table.
indicators.why: DDR4 16Gb spot is now below the $82 trigger and DDR5 posted its first small decline: spot has stopped rising, though contract and HBM pricing are still firm.
indicators.watch: DDR5 16Gb spot below $60; October contract figures; Samsung and SK hynix 2027 HBM4 pricing.
indicators.note: Changed since Nov 2: DDR4 spot -0.8c to $81.93 (below the $82 watch level), DDR5 -0.17c. Signal moved to neutral.

indicators.name: Power and permitting bottleneck for AI data centres
indicators.value: Nov 3 election: Democrats won Congress and Gina Hinojosa won Texas governor on a pledge for an immediate data-centre moratorium (not yet law). Texas holds about 25-30% of planned US data-centre GW (Wells Fargo, Ives); Bernstein puts about 244 GW (56% of the pipeline) as politically exposed but calls the risk overstated. More than 30 local ballot measures restricting data centres passed (Semafor). TCEQ permit pause still in force.
indicators.why: The bottleneck moved from grid physics to politics: the largest US build state elected a governor promising to pause new sites.
indicators.watch: Texas legislature timing for any moratorium; PJM large-load compliance filing (~Nov 9); ERCOT/PUCT audit by Dec 10; VRT, GEV, BE reaction.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct: election result added; VRT -14%, GEV -10%, BE -8% intraday Nov 4.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capex vs cloud backlog
indicators.value: AMD Q4 guide about $17B (+66% y/y) with data centre $8.5B in Q3 (+97%); Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and Anthropic running on Helios. Amazon keeps 2026 capex about $220B and 2027 'meaningfully more'; AWS backlog $578B. Hyperscalers rallied 3-7% Nov 4.
indicators.why: Supplier guides keep rising, so the buyers are still signing; the market rewarded hyperscalers and punished their suppliers on Nov 4.
indicators.watch: Nvidia Nov 17 guide; CoreWeave Nov 10 backlog; any 2027 capex number or cut tied to free cash flow.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 30: AMD guide added; ALAB Q4 guide $730-750M also above consensus.

indicators.name: Neocloud credit: CoreWeave CDS and bonds
indicators.value: CoreWeave CDS widened again Nov 4 (CNBC, no level published); last confirmed level about 1,041bp on Oct 27 (Markit), off the 1,194.5bp record. Shares fell 6-7% Nov 4; Citi cut its target to $128 from $159 (Buy kept). Neocloud stocks about -6%.
indicators.why: The financing leg is still the weak point, and Texas policy risk falls hardest on borrowers building new sites.
indicators.watch: CoreWeave Q3 Nov 10 (funding, depreciation, backlog); 9.75% 2031 notes below 75c; Nvidia's reported debt guarantee for Nscale.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 26: spread eased late October, then widened on the election; exact Nov 4 level not found.

indicators.name: Nvidia data-centre demand signals
indicators.value: Q3 FY27 results confirmed for Tue Nov 17 (call 5:00pm ET). FT (Nov 3): Nvidia asking cloud partners to sell at least 51% of new capacity to non-Chinese customers. The Information (Oct 30): Nvidia in talks to guarantee debt for Nscale's Anthropic site in West Virginia. Stock about -1% Nov 4.
indicators.why: Demand is not in question (AMD, ALAB guides), but Nvidia is increasingly backstopping customers' financing, which ties its results to neocloud credit.
indicators.watch: Nov 17 data-centre revenue, gross margin and customer concentration; any formal Nscale guarantee; CFTC GPU-futures outcome Nov 9.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 27: earnings date confirmed; China 51% rule and Nscale guarantee talks added.
